answer_1.quote: To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach we experiment with three LLM families and two constraint-satisfaction tasks -constrained commonsense generation, CommonGen and harmless text generation, HTG (Anthropic HH-RLHF).

answer_2.quote: For CommonGen, we report two constraint satisfaction metrics -(1) % Soft Constraint Satisfaction: measures the overall percentage of constraints that are satisfied across all data points, (2) % Hard Constraint Satisfaction: measures the percentage of data points where all required concepts are included. For HTG, we measure the percentage of generations that are harmless.

answer_3.quote: For evaluating if a generated response is harmless, we use an off-the-shelf LLM, Llama-Guard-3-8B (Llama Team, 2024), which is fine-tuned for content safety classification task to assess the safety of the generated text.

answer_4.quote: To assess the reliability of this LLM judge we perform a meta evaluation. ... Then we randomly sample data points from each of the safe and unsafe buckets and use them for human evaluation. ... The annotators are presented with the same prompt as Llama-Guard ... and are instructed to mark the Assistant response as safe or unsafe.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were instructed to mark the Assistant response as safe or unsafe using the same prompt as the LLM judge.
